chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nazr ibn Soweed, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Zar’at, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (peace be upon him) that God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
“There is a rank in Heaven which no one but a just leader, intimate and kind relative, or a patient husband can attain.”

key_terms.ذُو رَحِمٍ وَصُولٌ: Intimate and kind relative (one who maintains kinship ties)
key_terms.ذُو عِيَالٍ صَبُورٌ: Patient husband/provider (one who patiently supports his dependents)

ai.seo_question: What are the three specific qualities required to attain a unique rank in Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the spiritual merit of three distinct virtues: just leadership (*Imam al-Adl*), kinship maintenance (*Silat al-Rahim*), and patient provision (*Sabr* in supporting dependents). In Shia tradition, these categories encompass both political authority and domestic piety, illustrating that high ranks in Paradise are attainable through diverse forms of righteous conduct.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-39 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nazr ibn Soweed, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Zar’at, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“There is a rank in Heaven which no one but a just leader, intimate and kind relative, or a patient husband can attain.”
